audits.title: Acute asthma in a children's emergency room: a clinical audit and management guideline proposal.
audits.setting: Children's emergency room, Lagos University Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Triggers, current medication and severity not documented in 73.3%, 93.3% and 96.7%; discharge medication not given in 70.0% and clinic follow-up not arranged in 93.3%.

audits.other_findings: Nebulised salbutamol and oral steroids given in 80.0%, but aminophylline often added; a guideline and protocol-based records were proposed.
audits.citation: Okoromah CA, Renner JK, Oduwole AO, Adenuga AO. Acute asthma in a children's emergency room: a clinical audit and management guideline proposal. Niger Postgrad Med J. 2006;13(4):348-353. doi:10.4103/1117-1936.180884. PMID: 17203130.

audits.title: Suboptimal asthma care for immigrant children: results of an audit study.
audits.standard: Review criteria derived from clinical asthma guidelines
audits.setting: Paediatric department, Academic Medical Centre Amsterdam and six regional primary care centres

cycle1.result: Ethnic differences in suboptimal care were not significant; 'other non-Western' children more often received suboptimal care.

audits.other_findings: Nature of suboptimal care differed: under-prescribing, poor information exchange between physicians, or lack of education and counselling.
audits.citation: Urbanus-van Laar JJ, de Koning JS, Klazinga NS, Stronks K. Suboptimal asthma care for immigrant children: results of an audit study. BMC Health Serv Res. 2008;8:22. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-8-22. PMID: 18218104.

audits.title: Children admitted with acute wheeze/asthma during November 1998-2005: a national UK audit.
audits.setting: UK-wide annual audit of children over 1 year admitted with acute wheeze/asthma, 53-67 centres per year

cycle1.result: In 1998, 7% of admitted children received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 24% were discharged with a written asthma plan.

cycle2.result: By 2005, 44% received bronchodilators exclusively by spacer and 41% were discharged with a written asthma plan.

audits.other_findings: 9429 admissions over 8 annual audits; around 90% received systemic steroids and wide variation between centres in chest x-rays and written plans. Children under respiratory specialists more often had documented asthma education, plans and inhaler technique checks.
audits.citation: Davies G, Paton JY, Beaton SJ, Young D, Lenney W. Children admitted with acute wheeze/asthma during November 1998-2005: a national UK audit. Arch Dis Child. 2008;93(11):952-958. doi:10.1136/adc.2007.133868. PMID: 18499775.

audits.title: Childhood asthma in the emergency department: an audit.

cycle1.result: Deficiencies in recording systolic blood pressure (14%), conscious level (30%) and peak flow (46%). Correct β2 agonist dose 96%, oral or IV steroid 82%; about 50% had repeat vital signs; 36% discharged with the correct prednisolone dose.

audits.intervention: Improved integrated care pathway suggested (not re-audited)
audits.citation: Wilder C, Shiralkar S. Childhood asthma in the emergency department: an audit. Int Emerg Nurs. 2015;23(2):197-202. doi:10.1016/j.ienj.2014.09.001. PMID: 25263689.

audits.title: Audit of acute asthma management at the Paediatric Emergency Department at Wad Madani Children's Hospital, Sudan.
audits.setting: Paediatric Emergency Department, Wad Madani Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: Deficient initial severity assessment; salbutamol use consistent with guidelines, but inhaler delivery method inappropriate for age, no ipratropium and heavy antibiotic use (no figures given).

audits.other_findings: Little effort on prophylaxis, education, emergency planning or follow-up at discharge.
audits.citation: Ibrahim SM, Haroun HM, Ali HM, Tag Eldeen IE. Audit of acute asthma management at the Paediatric Emergency Department at Wad Madani Children's Hospital, Sudan. Sudan J Paediatr. 2012;12(1):104-114. PMID: 27493337.

audits.title: Management of children and young people (CYP) with asthma: a clinical audit report.
audits.standard: National Review of Asthma Deaths (NRAD) recommendations
audits.setting: Harrow Clinical Commissioning Group primary care

cycle1.result: Risks for future attacks not recognised, few assessed objectively during attacks and only 10% of attacks followed up within 2 days.

audits.other_findings: Hospital admissions in children and young people fell by 16% after the audit.
audits.citation: Levy ML, Ward A, Nelson S. Management of children and young people (CYP) with asthma: a clinical audit report. NPJ Prim Care Respir Med. 2018;28(1):16. doi:10.1038/s41533-018-0087-5. PMID: 29785053.

audits.title: A Retrospective Audit of Pharmacologic and Non-Pharmacologic Management of Childhood Acute Asthma Exacerbation at Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto: Adherence to Global Treatment Guidelines.
audits.standard: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) guidelines (17 major recommendations)
audits.setting: Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto

cycle1.result: Of 17 GINA recommendations, adherence was good for 5 (29.4%), moderate for 7 (41.2%) and poor for 5 (29.4%); moderate adherence in 61 (96.8%) and poor in 2 (3.2%) patients.

audits.other_findings: Most were discharged on a short course of oral corticosteroid only (58.8%).

audits.title: Effectiveness of Pediatric Asthma Pathways in Community Hospitals: A Multisite Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: Evidence-based asthma pathway measures (e.g. systemic corticosteroids within 60 mins, tobacco smoke screening)
audits.setting: Emergency departments and inpatient units of 2 community hospitals

cycle1.result: Pre-pathway: timely steroids 32% (Site 1) and 62% (Site 2); tobacco screening 82% and 54%; CXR use 44% (Site 1); antibiotics 23% (Site 2); ED LOS 230 mins (Site 1).

audits.intervention: Asthma pathway implementation with local champions, educational meetings, audit and feedback and EHR integration.

cycle2.result: Post-pathway: timely steroids 57% and 75%; tobacco screening 100% and 89%; CXR 29%; antibiotics 3%; ED LOS 197 mins.

audits.other_findings: 881 ED visits and 138 hospitalisations analysed; no significant change in other outcomes.
audits.citation: Desai M, Caldwell K, Gupta N, Bekmezian A, Cabana MD, Auerbach AD, et al.. Effectiveness of Pediatric Asthma Pathways in Community Hospitals: A Multisite Quality Improvement Study. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(6):e355. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000355. PMID: 33134758.

audits.title: Improving management of acute asthma in children through an integrated care pathway.
audits.standard: Evidence-based practice: bronchodilator by metered-dose inhaler with holding chamber, Pulmonary Score documentation and symptom control assessment
audits.setting: Primary care centres in two health districts and a regional paediatric emergency department (Cruces University Hospital)

cycle1.result: MDI with holding chamber 9.0% in primary care and 31.5% in the PED; Pulmonary Score documented 16.3% and 48.4%; symptom control assessed 8.0% and 32.9%.

audits.intervention: Co-designed asthma integrated care pathway with training, electronic decision support, family education and regular audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: MDI with holding chamber 26.7% in primary care and 61.4% in PED; Pulmonary Score 45.1% and 78.7%; symptom control assessment 23.4% and 67.4%.

audits.other_findings: 7241 acute asthma episodes in total; no change in PED length of stay, admissions or revisits.
audits.citation: Montejo M, Paniagua N, Pijoan JI, Saiz-Hernando C, Castelo S, Martin V, et al.. Improving management of acute asthma in children through an integrated care pathway. BMJ Paediatr Open. 2026;10(1):e004105. doi:10.1136/bmjpo-2025-004105. PMID: 41663148.

audits.title: Management of Paediatric Acute Asthma in a Metropolitan Emergency Department: A Retrospective Audit.
audits.standard: Sydney Children's Hospital Network Asthma-Acute Management Practice Guideline
audits.setting: Metropolitan emergency department, Sydney Children's Hospital Network (Fairfield Hospital)

cycle1.result: Severity documentation incomplete (speech 78%, cyanosis 69%); chest X-ray in 34.6%; mean bronchodilator burst longer than recommended (salbutamol 46.7 min, ipratropium 47.7 min); systemic steroids in 92% with appropriate dose in 63%; IV magnesium in 8/27 (29.6%) severe or life-threatening cases.

audits.other_findings: 56 (36.6%) admitted; mean ED stay 6.5 h admitted vs 4.3 h discharged.
audits.citation: Toufaili Y, Sarukkali N. Management of Paediatric Acute Asthma in a Metropolitan Emergency Department: A Retrospective Audit. J Paediatr Child Health. 2026;62(8):1394-1402. doi:10.1111/jpc.70446. PMID: 42186127.

audits.title: Asthma: audit of peak flow rate guidelines for admission and discharge.
audits.standard: Admission and discharge guidelines based on peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR)
audits.setting: Casualty department, National Children's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Children admitted with PEFR >= 40% expected after treatment: 43% (44/101); with PEFR > 60%: 23% (12/52).

audits.intervention: Introduction of PEFR-based admission and discharge guidelines.

cycle2.result: Children admitted with PEFR >= 40% expected: 26% (38/145); with PEFR > 60%: 5% (4/80).

audits.other_findings: No significant change in reattendance rate.
audits.citation: Taylor MR. Asthma: audit of peak flow rate guidelines for admission and discharge. Arch Dis Child. 1994;70(5):432-434. doi:10.1136/adc.70.5.432. PMID: 8017968.

audits.title: Pathways for Improving Inpatient Pediatric Asthma Care (PIPA): A Multicenter, National Study.
audits.standard: Evidence-based inpatient asthma care pathway measures (early metered-dose inhaler use, tobacco screening and referral, length of stay)
audits.setting: 85 children's and community hospitals in a national learning collaborative

cycle1.result: Baseline chart review of up to 20 charts per month per hospital (figures not reported).

audits.intervention: Pathway implementation with local champions, external mentors, educational seminars, QI methods and audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Early metered-dose inhaler use OR 1.18 (95% CI 1.14-1.22); referral to smoking cessation OR 1.93 (1.27-2.91); length of stay unchanged (RR 1.00).

audits.other_findings: 68 of 85 hospitals completed; 65% improved in at least one outcome; no change in readmissions or revisits.
audits.citation: Kaiser SV, Jennings B, Rodean J, Cabana MD, Garber MD, Ralston SL, et al.. Pathways for Improving Inpatient Pediatric Asthma Care (PIPA): A Multicenter, National Study. Pediatrics. 2020;145(6):e20193026. doi:10.1542/peds.2019-3026. PMID: 32376727.

audits.title: Pathways to Improve Pediatric Asthma Care: A Multisite, National Study of Emergency Department Asthma Pathway Implementation.
audits.standard: Asthma pathway measures, primarily systemic corticosteroid within 60 minutes of arrival
audits.setting: 83 children's and community hospital emergency departments

cycle1.result: Baseline monthly chart review of up to 20 charts (figures not reported).

audits.intervention: Pathway implementation with local champions, external mentors, educational seminars and audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Corticosteroid within 60 minutes aOR 1.26 (95% CI 1.02-1.55); triage severity assessment aOR 1.88 (1.22-2.90).

audits.other_findings: No change in chest radiograph use or ED length of stay; 61 of 83 EDs completed.
audits.citation: Kaiser SV, Johnson MD, Walls TA, Teach SJ, Sampayo EM, Dudley NC, et al.. Pathways to Improve Pediatric Asthma Care: A Multisite, National Study of Emergency Department Asthma Pathway Implementation. J Pediatr. 2020;223:100-107.e2. doi:10.1016/j.jpeds.2020.02.080. PMID: 32409021.

audits.title: A case audit of acute severe asthma in children.

cycle1.result: Major deficiencies in recording basic data for managing the acute attack; drug prescribing consistently accurate.

audits.other_findings: Oxygen and nebulisation regimens poorly recorded; discharge letters often lacked follow-up information.
audits.citation: Dawson KP, Mogridge N. A case audit of acute severe asthma in children. Aust Clin Rev. 1986;6(23):200-203. PMID: 3579729.
